newsitem.title: USA: NYS Scanlon says MTA/NYC proceed use inappropriate.
newsitem.headline: NYS Scanlon says MTA/NYC proceed use inappropriate.

text.p: New York State Deputy Comptroller for New York City Rosemary Scanlon said Tuesday the proposed use of proceeds by the city from a bond sale for Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) "inappropriate."

Scanlon, testifying here before the city's Office of Management and Budget on the city's debt affordability, said she has expressed concern about the city's proposed transaction with the MTA regarding the sale of the New York Coliseum, which is included in the fiscal year 1998 budget, which starts July 1.

The city, under an agreement with MTA, is allowed to utilize the proceeds from the Coliseum sale for general operating expenses contingent upon the city issuing bonds in a like amount to fund the Transit Authority capital program.

"I belive the treatment of the sale proceeds in this manner is inappropriate, since the city's commitment to issue debt for the MTA capital plan is based on its intention to use the proceeds in its operating budget," Scanlon said.
